We ignore the experience of being together with our friends when we talk with them too much

I believe the issue has less to do with "ignoring the experience of being together" and more to do with "misunderstanding how to make the most of the experience".

For instance, when I see a close friend for the first time in a while, I'm usually anxious to catch up with them and bring up certain conversation topics. I also feel pressure to hit on all the points I wanted to bring up with them (their new job, their thoughts on X topic, etc). Sometimes this leads to a virtual to-do list for my time with them. Instead, we could focus on enjoying each other's company, appreciating the thoughts the other has (regardless of whether we have time to hear ALL of them), and being happy with the time we do have.

I fall victim to this a lot, and have been trying to focus a little more on soaking up the atmosphere of being around friends I haven't seen in a while when I notice I'm playing this game. The organic flow that can happen when you apply a little mindfulness to the present moment and the thoughts that your current situation engenders as opposed to looking backwards too much can be pretty surprising and awesome.
